newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares slip on prospects of mid-term polls.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares slip on prospects of mid-term polls.

text.p: Delhi shares slipped lower in afternoon trade on Friday on nervous selling as prospects of a mid-term elections brightened, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 10.10 points lower at 740.40 at 1:00 p.m. (0730 GMT).
"The market is flooded with nervous sellers," said Ashok Kaul of brokers Rajpaul Chadha and Company.
"Investors and speculators want to sell fast as they are afraid of prices falling further," he added.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda moved a vote of confidence in his government before the lower house of parliament. The vote was expected to be held after 8 p.m. (1430 GMT) on Friday.

Deve Gowda's chances of surviving the vote, with the support of his coalition's 178 votes, appeared thin as the Congress with its 140 votes and the rightwing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party, which controls 193 seats with allies, have vowed to vote against the motion.
Deve Gowda called the confidence vote after the Congress party withdrew its make-or-break support for his minority coalition government.
Reliance Industries fell 5.20 rupees to 376.00, brokers said.
Larsen and Toubro shed 4.20 rupees to 206.50.
State Bank of India quoted 8.55 rupees lower at 266.00
